verses.1: And after that, the sons of Moab and the sons of Ammon came along with them. They also joined forces with the people of Ammon against Joshua.
verses.2: And they came and said to Joshua, “The enemy has come against us. They are far away from us, beyond the sea, from Aram. They are in Timnah. It’s a place where there are many eyes.”
verses.3: And Joshua saw that he had given his face to God. He then issued a commandment for all the Jews.
verses.4: And the Jews gathered together to ask God for help. From all the cities of Judah, they came to ask God for assistance.
verses.5: And Joshua stood in the midst of the Jewish people and in Jerusalem, in the house of God, before the new courtyard.
verses.6: And the LORD, our God, said, “You are indeed the God of heaven. You rule over all the nations. In your hands lie power and greatness. There is no one who can stand against you.”
verses.7: Now, you, our God, have received possession of this land from before your people, Israel. You have given it to the descendants of Abraham for eternal possession.
verses.8: And they settled there and built it for you, as a holy place for your name. As it is written.
verses.9: If evil shall come upon us, with destruction, famine, and death, then let it stand before this house. And before you, for your name is in this house. We will cry out to you for help from our troubles. May you hear and save us.
verses.10: And now, behold, the hills of Ebal, Moab, and the mountain of Seir—places that were not given to Israel when they came out of Egypt. They abandoned those places, and they were never destroyed again.
verses.11: And behold, they are coming against us to take us away from your city, which you have given us as a inheritance.
verses.12: Our God, do not judge them! We don’t have the strength to face this great trial that has befallen us. We don’t know what will happen to us. Our eyes are witnesses of it.
verses.13: And all of Judah stood before Jehovah, with their wives and children also.
verses.14: And Ezeriel, son of Zacharias, son of Benyah, son of Yehiyal, son of Matanya the Levite, from the sons of Asaf. The spirit of Jehovah was upon him among the crowd.
verses.15: And he said, “Let all the Jews and the inhabitants of Jerusalem listen to this. Let the king also listen to what the LORD has said to you. Do not be afraid, nor tremble before this great enemy. For it is not your battle; it is a battle for God.”
verses.16: After that, they climbed up onto the hill. You could find them at the end of the stream, right by the shore of the Yeruval Sea.
verses.17: Do not fight against this. Stand firm and see the salvation of Jehovah with you. Judah and Jerusalem shall be saved. Do not be afraid, and do not be discouraged. Then go ahead, and Jehovah will be with you.
verses.18: And Joshua ruled over the land and all of Judah. The inhabitants of Jerusalem fell down before Jehovah, to worship Him.
verses.19: And the Levites stood up from among the descendants of the Kohathites and the Korhites, to praise the LORD God of Israel with a loud voice.
verses.20: In the morning, they gathered together and went out to the desert. As they left, Joshua stood up and said, “Hear me, Jews! And you who live in Jerusalem, believe in your God. Believe also in His prophets and succeed in doing what He commands.”
verses.21: And he commanded the people to stand up in prayer before Jehovah. They praised and glorified the Holy One, as they prepared to go forth. They said, “Praise Jehovah, for His kindness lasts forever.”
verses.22: And at the time when they began to fight and battle, Jehovah gave many people from the people of Moab and from Mount Seir who came to Judea. They were defeated.
verses.23: And the sons of Amnon and Moab stood on top of the inhabitants of Mount Seir, ready to destroy them. And along with them, all those who lived in Seir also helped their fellow man in their destruction.
verses.24: And Judah came up onto the plateau overlooking the sea. They turned towards the mountains, but they were covered with dead bodies lying on the ground. There was no one to save them.
verses.25: And Joshua and his people went in and plundered their possessions. They found plenty of goods, livestock, and all kinds of delicious foods. They took them for themselves without paying any price. For three days they plundered the people’s possessions, because there was so much wealth there.
verses.26: And on the fifth day, they gathered together in that place of blessing. For there, they praised Jehovah. Therefore, they called that place “Emek Baracha” until today.
verses.27: And every Jew returned to Jerusalem. They rejoiced because Jehovah was happy with them after their enemies had been defeated.
verses.28: And they went into Jerusalem in boats and in ships, to the house of Jehovah.
verses.29: And there was fear in heaven over all the kings of the earth, when they heard that Jehovah was fighting against Israel’s enemies.
verses.30: And the kingdom of Jehosaphat became peaceful. Then its gods were sent to him from around it.
verses.31: Jehosaphat ruled over Judah for thirty-five years. He also ruled in Jerusalem for forty-five years. His mother’s name was Azubah, daughter of Shilhi.
verses.32: And he walked in the way of his father Abraham, and did not turn away from it to do what was right in the eyes of Jehovah.
verses.33: But the idols did not vanish, and the people still did not prepare their hearts for the God of their ancestors.
verses.34: And the additional words of Josaphat, the first and later kings, are written in the words of Jehoshaphat son of Hananiah. He compiled them into a book of the kings of Israel.
verses.35: And after that, Jehosaphat, king of Judah, made peace with Ahaziah, king of Israel. But Ahaziah was a wicked man who did evil deeds.
verses.36: And he took him with him to do some work related to traveling to Tarshish. They carried out those tasks with great effort and diligence.
verses.37: Eliyahu, son of Dodavah, was taken captive by Mordecai to Jeremiah. Jeremiah said, “Since you have dealt treacherously with Ahaziah, the LORD will bring about your downfall. Your plans will fail, and you won’t be able to go to Tarshish.”
